This integration brings the **YoLink** devices (YoSmart) of a YoLink hub into
Gladys, through the **official YoLink Open API v2**: the same account as the
YoLink app, no hack. Unofficial, not affiliated with YoSmart.

> **Development version (0.1).** Written from the official documentation
> (doc.yosmart.com) and YoSmart's official Python library `yolink-api`,
> tested with simulated answers, not yet with real devices. Feedback is
> welcome on the GitHub repository.

## What you get

One Gladys device per supported YoLink device:

| YoLink device                                          | In Gladys                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Door sensor (DoorSensor)                               | open/closed, battery %                                           |
| Motion sensor (MotionSensor)                           | motion, battery %                                                |
| Leak sensor (LeakSensor)                               | water leak, battery %                                            |
| Temperature & humidity sensor (THSensor)               | temperature °C, humidity % (not on probe-less models), battery % |
| Vibration sensor (VibrationSensor)                     | vibration, battery %                                             |
| Plug, switch (Outlet, Switch)                          | on/off (settable), power W (Energy plugs)                        |
| Power strip (MultiOutlet)                              | each socket on/off (settable)                                    |
| Water valve (Manipulator, LeakStop, FlowSmart Control) | valve open/closed (settable), battery %                          |
| Lock (Lock M1, Lock M2)                                | locked (settable), battery %                                     |
| Siren (Siren)                                          | siren on/off (settable), battery %                               |
| Garage door (GarageDoor, Finger)                       | cover command open/close, state from its door sensor             |

Hubs, remotes, thermostats, sprinklers and other types are not supported yet:
the **Test the connection** button tells how many devices are skipped.

## Installation

1. In the YoLink app: **Account** > **Advanced Settings** > **Personal Access
   Credentials**, then **+** to make one. Note its **UAID** and **secret key**.
2. Install the integration from the Gladys store.
3. In the **Configuration** tab, enter the UAID and the secret key, then save.
   The status reads "Connected to YoLink: 12 devices. Live events on."
4. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the devices you want. Their values
   arrive as soon as they are added.

## Safety: commands off by default

These commands are refused until you allow them in the configuration:

| Option                         | Default | Off: Gladys…                             |
| ------------------------------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Allow unlocking the locks      | no      | can lock, never unlock                   |
| Allow opening the garage doors | no      | can close a door its sensor reports open |
| Allow opening the water valves | no      | never opens a valve                      |
| Allow closing the water valves | no      | never closes a valve                     |
| Allow stopping the sirens      | yes     | can start a siren, never stop it         |

A refused command shows a message pointing to the option. To shut the water
off from a scene on a leak, turn on "Allow closing the water valves". A siren
whose stopping is off stops by itself after the alarm duration set in the
YoLink app.

A YoLink garage door appears in Gladys as a **cover command** (like a
shutter: open, close), never as a switch, so a scene that turns everything on
or off never reaches it. The YoLink controller itself only knows "toggle":

- **stop** is refused: the controller cannot stop the door, and a toggle sent
  instead could reverse it;
- just before toggling, the integration reads the paired door sensor again;
  when there is none, or it is offline or gives no state, the command is
  refused (a toggle could do the opposite);
- Gladys waits 5 seconds for the answer of a command: a garage command that is
  not ready to be sent 3.5 seconds after it arrived (slow sensor, another
  command of that garage in progress) is refused and nothing is sent;
- the commands of one garage run one at a time; after a toggle, any new
  command of that garage is refused with a "command ignored" message for 60
  seconds or until the sensor reports a state other than the one before the
  toggle (an offline sensor does not end it): a second "close" sent while the
  door moves would open it again;
- **limit**: a door already moving by other means (remote, wall button, the
  YoLink app) may be reversed by a "close" from Gladys, because the YoLink API
  cannot tell that it moves: the sensor only says "open" or "closed";
- **limit**: a sensor that is wrong (badly placed, magnet out of line, state
  stuck) makes the toggle do the opposite of the command, a "close" that
  **opens** the door included, even with opening turned off. This cannot be
  detected: the cloud only returns the last state the sensor reported. Check
  that the sensor follows the door before automating.

## How the values arrive

- **Live** ("Live events" option, on by default): the integration subscribes
  to the MQTT events of your YoLink home. A door opening, a motion or a leak
  arrive within a second or two. Every alert is recorded, even two alerts in a
  row. Read "Privacy" before leaving it on.
- **Full refresh**: at start, then every 30 minutes (10 to 1440), the
  integration reads the device list and the state of each device again over
  HTTPS (one request per device, half a second apart). Without the live
  events, this is the only source of the values.
- The devices of the European zone ("-EC" models) are read on YoLink's EU
  cloud, the others on the US cloud, as the app does.
- YS6801 power strip: channel 0 is the USB ports, channels 1 to 4 are sockets
  1 to 4.

## Usage limits

- YoLink allows one access credential 5 open MQTT connections and 10 new
  connections per 5 minutes: the integration uses one per cloud (two at most)
  and never opens more than 8 per 5 minutes. Do not share one credential
  between several programs (Home Assistant, Gladys…): make one per program.
- When YoLink answers "limits reached", the integration pauses for 15
  minutes, during which neither Discovery nor the test button reads YoLink; on
  a network error it retries after 1, 2, 5, 10 then 15 minutes.
- Gladys accepts 300 states per minute: beyond, the values wait for the next
  minute.

## Options

| Option                          | Default | Role                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| UAID, secret key                | —       | the access credential made in the YoLink app   |
| Allow unlocking, garage, valves | no      | see "Safety"                                   |
| Allow stopping the sirens       | yes     | see "Safety"                                   |
| Live events (unencrypted MQTT)  | yes     | see "Privacy"                                  |
| Full refresh interval (min)     | 30      | how often everything is read again             |
| Language of the feature names   | French  | feature names of the devices added from now on |

## Troubleshooting

- **"YoLink refused the UAID or the secret key"**: check them (the credential
  may have been deleted in the app). The integration waits for a change or a
  click on **Test the connection**.
- **`cloud` badge with an orange dot "Live events paused"**: the MQTT
  connection dropped, the integration reconnects (30 s, then up to 5 min).
  The values arrive at the next refresh at the latest.
- **`unreachable` badge with an orange dot**: YoLink reports the device
  offline (batteries, hub range).
- **"The LeakStop did not answer"**: in its power-saving (class A) mode it
  only listens from time to time; try again, or change its mode in the YoLink
  app.
- **A device is missing**: its type is not supported yet; open an issue on
  the GitHub repository with its model. The FlowSmart Meter (YS5007), which
  has no valve, is skipped.

## Privacy

The UAID and the secret key are kept by Gladys in its database (the key is
masked in the interface, never shown again; Gladys does not encrypt it, so it
is in its backups too). The key is only sent to
`api.yosmart.com/open/yolink/token` (HTTPS) to get an access token, which stays
in memory (nothing is written to `/data`). Every other HTTP request (device
list, states, commands) goes to YoLink over HTTPS.

### Live events: what travels in clear

The "Live events" option is **on by default**. It is the only part of the
integration that is **not encrypted**: YoLink's MQTT broker only offers plain
TCP on port 8003 (port 8004 is WebSocket, without TLS too; a TLS connection is
refused on both).

- **Between what and what**: the machine running Gladys (the integration's
  container) and YoLink's MQTT broker, `mqtt.api.yosmart.com:8003` (US cloud)
  and, if you have European devices, `api-eu.yosmart.com:8003` (EU cloud),
  through your local network, your internet provider and the internet.
- **What travels in clear**:
  - the **access token** (sent as the MQTT user name at each connection). It
    is valid about 2 hours: whoever reads it can, during that time, **command
    every YoLink device of yours, unlocking the locks and opening the garage
    included**, whatever the Gladys options;
  - your YoLink **home id** (in the topic) and the **id of each device**;
  - **every event of your devices**: doors opening and closing, motions,
    leaks, temperatures and humidity, lock, valve, siren and plug states,
    batteries, the answers to commands. They tell when someone is at home.
- **Forged events**: without TLS, someone on that path can also inject fake
  events (a door opening, a leak, a motion) that Gladys takes as real, and so
  trigger your scenes.
- **No encrypted alternative**: YoSmart offers no TLS port (only 8003 TCP and
  8004 WebSocket, both in clear); turning the option off is the only way to
  avoid it.
- **What never goes there**: the UAID and the secret key, and the commands
  (always sent over HTTPS).
- **To turn it off**: in Gladys, **Integrations** > **YoLink** >
  **Configuration**, untick "Live events (unencrypted MQTT)" and save. The
  MQTT connections close at once and none is opened again; the values then
  arrive only at each full refresh, over HTTPS (lower "Full refresh interval"
  to 10 minutes for fresher values). The status then reads "Live events off".

YoLink is a trademark of YoSmart; this integration is not affiliated with
YoSmart.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt YoLink in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your YoLink account | `section` | Nein | Brings your YoLink devices into Gladys through the official YoLink Open API v2 (a YoLink hub is required): door, motion, water leak, temperature and humidity, and vibration sensors, plugs, switches and power strips, water valves, locks, sirens and garage doors, with their batteries. Changes arrive live (MQTT), and everything is read again every 30 minutes. In the YoLink app, open Account > Advanced Settings > Personal Access Credentials, add one, and copy its UAID and secret key here. Unlocking, opening the garage door and opening or closing a water valve stay off until you allow them below. Unofficial, not affiliated with YoSmart. |
| UAID | `string` | Ja |  |
| Secret key | `secret` | Ja |  |
| Allow unlocking the locks from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: Gladys can lock, never unlock. |
| Allow opening the garage doors from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: Gladys never sends an opening; it can close a door its sensor reports open. The controller can only toggle: if the sensor is wrong, or if the door is already closing by other means, a "close" can stop it or open it again (see the guide). |
| Allow opening the water valves from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: Gladys never opens a valve. |
| Allow closing the water valves from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: turn it on to cut the water from a scene (on a leak, for example). |
| Allow stopping the sirens from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | On by default. Off: Gladys can start a siren, never stop it (it stops after its own alarm duration). |
| Live events (unencrypted MQTT) | `boolean` | Nein | On by default. YoLink's MQTT (port 8003) has no encryption: between this Gladys and YoLink's broker (mqtt.api.yosmart.com, api-eu.yosmart.com for EU devices), the access token and every event of your devices (doors, motions, leaks, temperatures, lock and valve states, batteries) travel in clear over your network and the internet. Whoever reads the token can command every YoLink device (unlocking and the garage included) for about 2 hours. The secret key and the commands always go over HTTPS. Untick and save to turn it off: the values then arrive only at each full refresh, over HTTPS. |
| Full refresh interval (min) | `number` | Nein | How often the device list and every state are read again, in minutes (10 to 1440). Live events arrive in between. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | Nein | Used for the names of the features of the devices added from now on. |

## So installierst du YoLink in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: YoLink erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-yolink:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-yolink](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-yolink).

YoLink benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

YoLink ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
